sentences.text: Otodus is an extinct genus of mackerel sharks that lived globally from the Paleocene to the Pliocene.
These animals belong to the class Chondrichthyes, which includes sharks, rays, and skates.
All species are known from fossilized teeth, while four species are also known from fossilized vertebrae.
Estimates for the maximum length of O. megalodon vary between 20.3 meters and 24.3 meters.
The controversial species O. poseidoni was first described in 1999 and measures approximately 12 meters.
The genus Otodus was first described by Louis Agassiz in 1843.
At least two Otodus species used warm-water coastal nursery areas to give birth to their young.
A potential nursery area for O. obliquus was found in the Ganntour basin in Morocco.
Studies suggest a dietary shift from fish to marine mammals occurred in the evolutionary history of otodontid sharks, based on zinc enrichment patterns in their teeth.
The parent group of the genus Otodus is the family Otodontidae.
It is widely believed that Otodus originated from the genus Cretalamna due to similar tooth morphology.
Scientists believe Otodus evolved into the genus Carcharocles based on transitional fossil teeth.
A species found in Kazakhstan is considered an undescribed species and is likely Otodus sp.
Fossils of Otodus range from the Paleocene epoch to the Early Pliocene epoch.
The time range for Otodus is from the Turonian to the Chibanian, spanning 93.9 to 0.34 million years ago.
The species O. debrayi lived from the Early Eocene to the Middle Eocene epoch.
O. debrayi fossils date from 47.8 to 38 million years ago and have been found in Africa, North America, Central Asia, and Europe.
